summary: Any price can change the best one- or two-transaction schedule, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n prices in the worst case. The four-state dynamic program processes each price once.

optimality.argument: If an algorithm leaves some price unread, changing it can create a uniquely favorable buy or sale endpoint while all inspected values remain fixed. Exact computation therefore requires Omega(n) inspections in the worst case. The current algorithm applies four constant-time state transitions to each price, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: An unseen price can become an endpoint of the uniquely optimal one- or two-transaction schedule, so arbitrary positions cannot be skipped.
The implementation updates the four transaction-stage balances once for each price.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover two transactions, one transaction, and no profitable transaction; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
